approval_required_for: Any repair that changes pipeline replication, logical block ordering, scheduler policy, FIFO depth, backpressure semantics, transfer unit, or memory schedule.
Any architecture-level or major trusted-template change proposed after localization.
Any change to the exact user-supplied wrapper or simulation-source baseline; such a change must create a newly approved immutable baseline rather than continue the same repair loop.

Any future intentional numeric-policy or tolerance change must start a separately approved verification campaign with new immutable identities; changing or loosening tolerance during this repair loop is forbidden.

executable_actions.on_failure: Keep the refined third-layer contract unpromoted. Report the missing dependency, instrumentation field, or noncanonical-evidence barrier to verification_artifacts.cross_layer_evidence_gate_auditor; do not let local pipeline checks or a liveness-only candidate substitute for functional_sim.
executable_actions.rationale: Make the dynamic acceptance dependency explicit and prevent a structural case_multilayer_pipeline result, local smoke, or disconnected liveness run from satisfying board-system acceptance. The refinement also defines pre-run transfer expectations and board-visible instrumentation without changing model semantics, numeric policy, architecture, or wrapper sources.

consumes: exact sample-project wrapper and simulation-source hash manifest
executable_actions.on_failure: If an immutable identity, real target-model reference, complete in-scope weight binding, exact-wrapper hash, or simulator capability is absent, classify the result as a verification/harness capability failure rather than hardware correctness. If real RTL evidence exists, preserve the failed run and route it to causal localization. Do not proceed to derived acceptance or Vivado.
executable_actions.rationale: Produce the sole canonical dynamic evidence source using the exact discovered sample-project wrapper and simulation sources. Functional acceptance requires the same immutable checkpoint, stimulus, target-model reference, numeric policy and tolerance, semantic testbench, and complete Transformer-block weight bindings used by the DUT.

executable_actions.on_failure: Emit a failed classifier with the canonical run identity and earliest observed violating transaction or no-progress interval. Do not rerun an isolated smoke test, reinterpret wrong-order or wrong-count progress as a pass, or classify an instrumentation-invalid timeout as hardware deadlock; route the evidence to failure localization.
executable_actions.rationale: Generate all pipeline classifiers as immutable subviews of one board simulation. Each report must include the canonical run ID, raw trace hash, exact-wrapper hash, stimulus and checkpoint identities, and instrumentation-manifest hash; no classifier may invoke a disconnected replacement simulation.

executable_actions.on_failure: Do not issue or reuse a board promotion certificate and do not enable backend handoff. Identify the stale, missing, cross-run, out-of-scope, smoke-only, or failed evidence item and route only that evidence class to its owning specialist or causal localization path.
executable_actions.rationale: Block backend handoff unless all third-layer reports, including externally owned AXI/DDR reports, originate from the same exact-wrapper functional simulation and satisfy the immutable semantic contract. This is the acceptance barrier against local smoke and disconnected pipeline evidence.

executable_actions.on_failure: Keep the third layer failed and preserve the canonical evidence. Do not speculate about a code fix, reopen a lower layer, or label the failure pipeline-local without an earliest causal boundary and checker-valid repair context.
executable_actions.rationale: Use the canonical board trace to identify the earliest causal boundary before any repair. Classify the result as verifier/instrumentation failure, inter-block scheduler or buffering failure, externally rooted wrapper/AXI/DDR stall, or trace-supported contradiction of the connected single-layer certificate.

executable_actions.on_failure: Keep the repair unpromoted, retain the original immutable checkpoint, stimulus, reference, numeric policy, tolerance, testbench, expected-transfer contract, and wrapper hashes, and return the new tool trace to localization. Do not loosen tolerance, alter golden outputs, substitute a simplified wrapper, or skip to backend.
produces: rerun same-source order, count, valid_ready, watchdog, deadlock, numeric, and weight-consumption reports
executable_actions.rationale: When localization proves an inter-block scheduler, replication, FIFO, progress-counter, or valid/ready implementation violation, apply a bounded template-constrained repair and rerun the complete board layer. Approval is required because a pipeline repair may affect replication, buffering, ordering, or scheduling. Immutable semantic and exact-wrapper identities must remain unchanged.

executable_actions.on_failure: Keep the board layer blocked and do not reopen or repair the single-layer or operator-leaf layer from an unsupported board symptom. Require a checker-valid earliest-boundary contradiction before backtracking.
executable_actions.rationale: A board failure may challenge reusable lower-layer evidence only when the canonical trace shows the earliest violation inside the connected block before the inter-block boundary. This action requests a bounded layer-2 replay rather than directly patching a leaf or bypassing the three-layer repair loop.

observations: The declared hierarchy follows the mandatory repair order: operator leaves, connected single Transformer layer, then the board AXI/DDR wrapped system. The third layer cannot execute or promote until the current-contract single-layer promotion certificate is valid.

The visible DAG already makes functional_sim a predecessor of case_multilayer_functional and case_pipeline_deadlock_check and places backend work after case_board_semantic_evidence. This is structurally aligned with board-wrapped simulation being canonical.

case_multilayer_pipeline must be interpreted only as construction, connectivity, scheduler-contract, expected-transfer-ledger, and instrumentation readiness. Its local or disconnected execution cannot prove dynamic block order, transfer completion, valid/ready correctness, or liveness.

The static data_order_trace_check result only confirms that Stage 3 order metadata is available. It is not dynamic board-system acceptance. deadlock_watchdog is correctly recorded as pending downstream and not_run.

The functional_sim evidence contract must bind one run identifier to the exact user-supplied sample-project wrapper and simulation-source hashes, simulator invocation and tool version, immutable checkpoint and complete Transformer-block-scoped tensor catalog, stimulus hash, target-model reference hash, numeric policy and fixed tolerance, semantic-testbench hash, loader/harness hash, and executed complete-scope DUT weight-consumption evidence.

Every pipeline event should carry cycle, boundary_id, logical_block_id, physical_slot_id, tx_id, token/tile/logical index, beat and lane identity, valid, ready, fire, last/end marker, occupancy or outstanding count, progress sequence, and completion state. These fields extend rather than replace the existing boundary trace fields.

Transfer counts must count accepted handshakes where fire equals valid and ready, not cycles where valid is merely asserted. At completion, observed accepted counts per boundary must equal a pre-run expected-transfer ledger derived from the immutable shape, block schedule, transfer unit, and testbench contract; transaction identities must show no skip, duplication, bypass, or reordering.

Block-order acceptance requires each transaction to traverse the declared logical Transformer-block sequence in order, while separately recording any time-multiplexed physical compute slot. A physical-slot reuse schedule must not be mistaken for logical block order.

Valid/ready acceptance requires no transfer unless valid and ready are simultaneously asserted, stable payload and transaction identity while valid is asserted under backpressure, conservation across declared buffers at completion, and no unexplained valid withdrawal, duplicated fire, or dropped terminal beat.

The watchdog window and legal no-progress intervals must be fixed before execution from the pipeline, buffering, latency, and tool contracts and must not be tuned from DUT output during repair. Progress includes accepted boundary transfers, declared internal retirement events, and relevant board-interface completions correlated from the canonical run.

Deadlock classification should distinguish completed, live/backpressured, pipeline deadlock, external wrapper/AXI/DDR starvation, progress-with-value/order/count failure, and unclassified timeout or invalid instrumentation. Only an incomplete run with no qualified progress beyond the fixed watchdog bound and a trace-supported pipeline wait cycle is a pipeline-deadlock finding.

The liveness-only VCS candidate and any local smoke test may support diagnostics but cannot populate the canonical functional_sim run identifier or satisfy case_multilayer_functional, transfer_count_check, deadlock_watchdog, case_pipeline_deadlock_check, or case_board_semantic_evidence.

The accelerator and golden boundary remain all target Transformer blocks only. Embedding/tokenization, final model norm, LM head/logits, sampling, and other model-tail work must not enter expected transfer counts, DUT weight coverage, or functional output comparison.

The authoritative SACG-memory summary reports zero active contamination barriers and zero open retry or backtrack requests. Missing downstream promotion certificates and real-tool runs are declared later-stage obligations, not current SACG-memory blockers.
proposed_actions: Materialize an explicit third-layer pipeline/liveness subgraph in which case_multilayer_pipeline only prepares the board-connected scheduler, instrumentation, and expected-transfer ledger.
Run one exact-wrapper board functional simulation after all immutable semantic prerequisites and current-contract lower-layer certificates are valid.
Derive block-order, transfer-count, valid/ready, progress, multi-layer functional, watchdog, and deadlock reports only from the canonical run manifest and raw trace hashes.
Require case_board_semantic_evidence to reject smoke, liveness-only, disconnected, stale, or cross-run evidence before backend handoff.
On a real trace failure, localize the earliest causal boundary before selecting verifier repair, pipeline-local repair, board-interface handoff, or trace-supported lower-layer backtrack.

Apply any approved pipeline repair without changing checkpoint, stimulus, target-model reference, numeric policy, tolerance, semantic testbench, expected transfer contract, or exact wrapper source identity; then rerun the entire board canonical evidence fanout.
risks: Evidence contamination risk: independently rerunning order, count, or deadlock checks could mix different wrapper, stimulus, checkpoint, RTL, or trace identities. Every classifier must reject evidence whose canonical run digest differs.
Data-order and shape risk: expected beat counts or logical block order derived from a different sequence bound, lane mapping, transfer unit, or block count can create false passes or false failures.
Flow-control risk: counting valid cycles instead of valid-and-ready fires can hide duplicated transfers, overcount backpressured beats, and misclassify progress.

Liveness risk: an unfrozen or wall-clock-based watchdog can classify legal compute or memory latency as deadlock, while a watchdog that treats counter toggles unrelated to accepted work as progress can conceal a real wait cycle.
Implementation/deployment risk: instrumentation attached only to a disconnected kernel or simplified wrapper would not observe board-wrapper backpressure and cannot support board-system acceptance.

Memory/runtime ownership risk: a no-progress root at the wrapper, AXI, or DDR boundary must be handed to the corresponding interface owner with correlated traces; it must not be labeled pipeline-local without an earliest causal pipeline boundary.

Lower-layer consistency risk: a board trace may contradict reusable single-layer evidence, but reopening layer 2 requires a bound earliest-violation trace. A third-layer symptom alone is insufficient for direct lower-layer repair.

Numeric-policy risk: order and liveness reports from one run must not be combined with value comparison from another run or with a changed tolerance. Checkpoint, stimulus, reference, tolerance, semantic testbench, and wrapper hashes remain immutable during repair.

Scope risk: including embedding, final norm, logits, or sampling traffic in transfer counts, weight coverage, or golden comparison would contaminate the Transformer-block accelerator acceptance boundary.

Conditional handoff risk: although the current artifact contract passed, omitting explicit canonical subviews for transfer_count_check and deadlock_watchdog could allow a downstream implementation to substitute local evidence unless the proposed refinement is materialized and audited.

edges: case_semantic_testbench + case_single_layer_semantic_evidence + case_multilayer_pipeline + case_board_interface_discovery + case_axi_ddr_interface -> functional_sim
functional_sim canonical run + case_multilayer_functional + deadlock_watchdog + transfer_count_check -> case_pipeline_deadlock_check
functional_sim canonical run -> case_axi_protocol_check and case_ddr_image_roundtrip under their owning specialists
local smoke, liveness-only, or disconnected pipeline checks -/-> case_board_semantic_evidence

Refine the third-layer subgraph so case_multilayer_pipeline is preparation-only, one immutable board simulation run is the sole canonical dynamic evidence source, and data-order, transfer-count, valid/ready, progress, watchdog, and deadlock results are hash-bound subviews of that run. Local smoke, liveness-only, or disconnected pipeline tests remain diagnostic and cannot contribute acceptance evidence. No active SACG-memory contamination barrier, retry request, or backtrack request is present, and no downstream simulation pass is claimed.
